title: Provider reconciliation effect settlement
description: Objective: land the missing @moe/runner authority that converts one canonical provider-run observation into the only effect terminal transition its evidence proves. Current measurement at HEAD 8557296330648bca2977e27d77fb0f26c319b758: public applyEffectCommand accepts a caller-selected settle target/outcomeClass; an executed public-root probe transitions ACTIVE to SUCCEEDED even when outcomeClass is HONEST_UNKNOWN, while no production reconciliation-to-effect mapper exists. Deliverable: a public-root settleEffectFromProviderObservation-style function and exact frozen evidence/failure contracts. It accepts an EffectIntent plus a closed provider observation (ProviderRunRef, source version/digest, provider terminal and infrastructure classifications, upstream refusal, observed completion instant), derives target/outcome/uncertainty/adoptedAt itself, invokes the production lifecycle reducer, and returns its exact terminal EffectIntent+EffectResult or typed refusal/MUST_DRAIN. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, provider-run storage/readers (task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8), release disposition, resource authority, new runtime command kinds, or physical launch. Consumer: task-1879166d7f12474fad8038e2a9d2433a. Verification: run `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` as separate foreground legs and record the nonzero test-count lines.
definitionOfDone: The @moe/runner public root exports one production settlement function whose exact input contains no effect target, outcomeClass, uncertainty, adoptedAt, result bytes, or terminal EffectIntent; it snapshots an EffectIntent plus a versioned provider observation and binds ProviderRunRef.effectIntentId to the intent before deriving anything.

A frozen exhaustive mapping covers every generated ProviderTerminalOutcome x ProviderInfrastructureOutcome case for ACTIVE and CANCEL_REQUESTED intents: only an infrastructure-clean proven completion/error may become SUCCEEDED/FAILED, clean cancellation reaches CANCELLED only from CANCEL_REQUESTED, ACTIVE cancellation returns the production MUST_DRAIN path, and every unproven combination stays UNKNOWN or refuses without authority. Tests assert the generated case count is nonzero and pin each exact terminal/refusal code and layer.

The implementation derives SettlementEvidence, UncertaintyEvidence, outcomeClass and adoptedAt solely from the admitted provider observation, then calls production applyEffectCommand; its returned EffectIntent and EffectResult are the reducer's exact frozen output. Malformed/foreign/unverifiable source evidence fails closed with distinct stable provider-settlement codes/layer, while reducer refusals retain their original SupervisorFailure code/layer.

Focused tests include the current counterexample (ACTIVE plus provider-unknown evidence can never produce SUCCEEDED), hostile/accessor inputs, effect/run binding mismatch, missing or unknown completion instant, terminal absorption, and one accepted completion control with exact result fields and digest. Mutating the production mapping to trust a caller target or map an unproven cell to success turns a named test red.

The curated runner surface and surface-ratchet test include the new values/types without deep imports; completion names task-1879166d7f12474fad8038e2a9d2433a as the consumer, and runner typecheck/test execute separately with nonzero Test Files and Tests counts.
taskRails: Never add a second effect reducer or construct EffectResult directly; derive a closed settle command and delegate to public applyEffectCommand, returning its output unchanged.

No caller-selected target, terminal state, outcomeClass, uncertainty, adoptedAt, result, or reconciliation verdict becomes authority. Provider facts are observations; unknown/unverifiable facts grant no terminal success authority.

Use the existing public ProviderRunRef, ProviderTerminalOutcome, ProviderInfrastructureOutcome, ProviderText, EffectIntent and lifecycle vocabularies; do not copy their literals into a daemon-local contract.

TDD exact stable code and refusing layer, positive generated-case counts, production-surface mutation drill, public-root surface ratchet, target <=250 physical lines per new production source, and explicit owned-path commit.

implementationPlan.description: Reproduce the counterexample before building anything, so the deliverable has a measured defect to close rather than a described one. Write a throwaway probe against the PUBLIC ROOT that calls `applyEffectCommand` with an ACTIVE intent, `target: "SUCCEEDED"` and `settlement.outcomeClass: "HONEST_UNKNOWN"`, run it, and record that it transitions to SUCCEEDED. Delete the probe in the same command. That recorded output is the exact behaviour DoD 4's counterexample test must forbid once the new function exists — and note carefully that this task does NOT change `applyEffectCommand`: rail 1 forbids a second reducer, so the reducer keeps accepting a caller-chosen target and the new function is what stops choosing one.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the four admitted cells and the fail-closed default, same test file. DoD 2 names exactly four rules and everything else is UNKNOWN-or-refuse: (a) infrastructure `NONE` + terminal `COMPLETED` may reach SUCCEEDED; (b) infrastructure `NONE` + terminal `ERROR_DURING_EXECUTION` may reach FAILED; (c) infrastructure `NONE` + terminal `CANCELLED` reaches CANCELLED ONLY from a CANCEL_REQUESTED intent; (d) an ACTIVE intent with a cancellation observation returns the production MUST_DRAIN path, which means issuing `requestCancel` and returning the reducer's `{kind: "MUST_DRAIN", drainRequired: true, versionDelta: 0}` UNCHANGED — `applyEffectCommand` already answers that for ACTIVE+requestCancel (effect-lifecycle.ts:211-218) and it is a third outcome kind, NOT a refusal, so a test matching on refusal codes here would be wrong. EXPLICIT AND DELIBERATE: `MAX_TURNS_EXHAUSTED` and `REFUSED` are terminal provider facts but are NOT "completion/error", so they may NEVER become SUCCEEDED or FAILED — they stay UNKNOWN. Pin that as its own named test, because it is the cell a future reader is most likely to "fix" toward FAILED. Every one of the remaining cells stays UNKNOWN or refuses without authority; assert an UNKNOWN settlement also carries the uncertainty evidence the reducer demands (`EFFECT_UNCERTAINTY_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED`, effect-lifecycle.ts:171-176).

implementationPlan.description: TDD the input contract, the binding, and the hostile arms. (a) THE INPUT SHAPE IS THE PROOF, per DoD 1: assert by exact key set that the admitted input contains NO `target`, `outcomeClass`, `uncertainty`, `adoptedAt`, result bytes or terminal EffectIntent — a substitute for derived authority must be UNREPRESENTABLE rather than validated away, the same discipline `FoundationVerificationRequest` uses. (b) BINDING: `ProviderRunRef.effectIntentId` must equal the snapshotted intent's `intentId`; a mismatch refuses with its own stable provider-settlement code and layer before anything is derived. Drive a case where the run ref is well-formed but names a foreign intent. (c) The completion instant: missing, and present-but-unknown (the `ProviderText` `{known: false}` arm), are two DISTINCT refusals — do not fold them, since one means nothing was recorded and the other means the provider recorded that it does not know. (d) HOSTILE INPUTS: accessor properties, `__proto__`, extra keys and a frozen input object; assert each refuses rather than letting a value survive into the derivation. (e) TERMINAL ABSORPTION: a snapshotted intent already terminal must surface the reducer's own `EFFECT_TERMINAL_ABSORBED` / `LIFECYCLE` pair unchanged — DoD 3 requires reducer refusals to retain their original SupervisorFailure code and layer, so assert both fields, not just that it refused.
implementationPlan.note: RED (EXIT=1, module still absent). Closed-vocabulary test pins the 9 codes and a nonzero length. DELIBERATE DEVIATION on plan 4(d)'s "frozen input object ... refuses": a frozen WELL-FORMED observation must be ADMITTED — refusing it would pin wrong behaviour and make the seam unusable for a careful caller. The test instead asserts a frozen observation yields an outcome equal to the mutable one, which is what actually proves no fact survived into a mutating derivation (a write-back would throw on the frozen record).

implementationPlan.description: TDD the accepted control with exact fields, and the counterexample. (a) ONE ACCEPTED COMPLETION CONTROL, as DoD 4 names: an infrastructure-clean proven completion on an ACTIVE intent returns the reducer's exact frozen `EffectIntent` and `EffectResult` — assert every `EffectResult` field by name (`resultVersion`, `intentId`, `terminalState`, `outcomeClass`, `settlementDigest`, `adoptedAt`) and assert the digest is the value the production derivation computed, not a hand-written constant. A refusal-only suite is blind to a wrong ACCEPTED value, which is why this control is not optional. Do not compute the expected digest by calling the production helper — that makes the assertion a tautology; derive it independently from the observation the test seeded. (b) THE COUNTEREXAMPLE FROM STEP 1, now as a permanent test: an ACTIVE intent plus provider-unknown evidence can NEVER produce SUCCEEDED. Assert the returned terminal is not SUCCEEDED AND that the outcome is the specific UNKNOWN-or-refusal the table declares, so the test cannot pass merely because some unrelated guard answered first.
implementationPlan.note: RED (EXIT=1, module still absent; test file now 579 lines — a test file, not a production source, so the per-FILE 250/400 production cap does not apply). Added (a) the ACCEPTED control: ACTIVE + COMPLETED + NONE asserts the whole EffectResult by name via toEqual — resultVersion "moe-effect-result/1", intentId, terminalState SUCCEEDED, outcomeClass PROVEN_RESULT, settlementDigest, adoptedAt — with the digest derived INDEPENDENTLY (canonicalDigest over a hand-transcribed {settlement, uncertainty:null} preimage), never by calling the derivation under test; plus the successor intent asserted as {...intent, state:"SUCCEEDED", version+1}, versionDelta 1, and Object.isFrozen on both. (b) the counterexample as a permanent test: ACTIVE + terminal UNKNOWN + infrastructure UNKNOWN asserts label === TERMINAL:UNKNOWN (the specific declared outcome, so an unrelated guard answering cannot make it pass), plus not SUCCEEDED, terminalState UNKNOWN, outcomeClass HONEST_UNKNOWN and the exact uncertainty-bearing digest. Also added a whole-sweep invariant: SUCCEEDED / FAILED / CANCELLED / MUST_DRAIN are each reached from EXACTLY ONE generated cell and 116 cells are UNPROVEN, which reddens on any table widening anywhere in the 120. Also pinned that the observed run epoch reaches the settlement digest (an epoch-drifted observation settles to a different digest) rather than being compared to EffectIntent.expectedGraphEpoch — those are counters from different domains and equating them would invent an authority this module has no basis for; the reasoning is in the test's own comment for QA.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
EXPORT FROM index.ts DIRECTLY, NOT THROUGH A NEW `surface/*` MODULE. `applyEffectCommand` and the whole effect-lifecycle family are already exported straight from `packages/runner/src/index.ts` (:118-125), so a sibling block is the consistent placement. It also sidesteps a guard that would otherwise fire nowhere near this code: `index-surface.test.ts:2214` pins `SURFACE_SOURCES.size` to 7 by reading the `surface/` directory, so a NEW `*-surface.ts` file reddens with a bare "expected 8 to be 7". Adding to an existing surface module was the alternative; rejected because none of the six is about effect settlement and the curated seams say plainly they must not grow on autopilot.

MAX_TURNS_EXHAUSTED AND REFUSED STAY UNKNOWN. Both are genuine terminal provider facts, and a reasonable reader will want to map them to FAILED. DoD 2 says only an infrastructure-clean proven COMPLETION or ERROR may become SUCCEEDED or FAILED, and rail 2 says unverifiable facts grant no terminal authority. So the fail-closed reading is that they are neither, and the plan makes that its own NAMED test precisely because it is the cell most likely to be "fixed" later.

THE MAPPING IS DECLARED AS DATA, not as branching. A 60-cell table written as conditionals cannot be swept exhaustively by the test without the test re-deriving the same conditions, which is the property-asserted-against-a-test-helper defect. As data, the test drives the real table.

NOT CHANGING applyEffectCommand. Rail 1 forbids a second reducer, and the reducer's willingness to accept a caller-chosen target is not itself the bug being fixed — the bug is that nobody derives the target from evidence. The reducer keeps its behaviour; this function stops anyone needing to choose.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD a42ae2f. The task cites HEAD 8557296; the premise re-measures TRUE, so it is not stale.

THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS REAL AND I FOUND ITS EXACT CAUSE. `settleIntent` (effect-lifecycle.ts:145-190) checks the admitted arc (:156), the settlement-evidence SHAPE (:162), and that an UNKNOWN target carries uncertainty evidence (:171). It NEVER compares `settlement.outcomeClass` to `command.target`, and `SettlementEvidence.outcomeClass` is typed as a bare `string` (effect-kernel.ts:237-241). So ACTIVE + target SUCCEEDED + outcomeClass HONEST_UNKNOWN is admitted. Nothing in packages/runner maps a provider observation to a justified target: `grep` finds HONEST_UNKNOWN only in the two provider cancel-reconcilers and a test fixture.

THE CASE COUNT IS DETERMINED, NOT ESTIMATED. `PROVIDER_TERMINAL_OUTCOMES` (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:37-39) has SIX members; `PROVIDER_INFRASTRUCTURE_OUTCOMES` (:48-51) has TEN. 6 x 10 = 60 cells, x 2 intent states = 120 generated cases. The sibling suite already asserts these counts by name (claude-telemetry-launch.test.ts:296 pins 10), so the convention exists.

SHAPES THE FUNCTION MUST COMPOSE. `EffectIntent` (effect-kernel.ts:185-199) carries state and version. `SettlementEvidence {reconciliationVersion, reconciliationDigest, outcomeClass}` (:237). `UncertaintyEvidence {uncertaintyReason, uncertaintyDigest}` (:243). `EffectResult {resultVersion, intentId, terminalState, outcomeClass, settlementDigest, adoptedAt}` (:255-262). `ProviderRunRef {provider: "claude", runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}` (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:141-147) — `effectIntentId` is the binding field DoD 1 names. `ProviderText = {known: true, value} | ProviderFactUnknown` (:138), which is why a missing completion instant and a known-unknown one are two different facts.

MUST_DRAIN IS NOT A REFUSAL. `applyEffectCommand` answers `{kind: "MUST_DRAIN", drainRequired: true, intent, versionDelta: 0}` for ACTIVE + requestCancel (effect-lifecycle.ts:211-218), and the module header (:34-36) is explicit that it is a third outcome kind because "a caller matching on refusal codes would retry a rejected command". Note also (:48-55) that ACTIVE -> CANCEL_REQUESTED IS an admitted row but is deliberately unreachable from a bare requestCancel; only the drain transaction authorises it.

THERE IS NO completion-instant FIELD in provider-telemetry-contracts today — grep for completedAt/completionInstant/observedAt returns nothing — so the new frozen observation contract owns it. That is a new field on a NEW contract, not a widening of a frozen upstream vocabulary, so rail 3 is satisfied.

PUBLICATION AND RATCHET. `applyEffectCommand` is exported directly from index.ts:121. The ratchet is `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(232)` (index-surface.test.ts:374) plus a sorted-name equality; the separate `SURFACE_SOURCES.size` guard at :2214 is pinned to 7 and fires only on a new `surface/*-surface.ts` FILE.

`expectTypeOf` IS A NO-OP HERE: packages/runner's test script is `vitest run --root ../.. packages/runner/src` with no `--typecheck`. Use a conditional-type assignment to pin a type-level fact; that IS enforced by the package typecheck because its tsconfig includes src/**/*.ts.

FILE SIZES: effect-lifecycle.ts 262, effect-kernel.ts 266 — both already over the 250 target, which is why the deliverable is a NEW module and neither is edited.

GATE RESOLVES: `@moe/runner` is packages/runner with typecheck and test scripts.
planningNotes.risks:
1. MUST_DRAIN READ AS A REFUSAL is the likeliest wrong turn. It returns a third outcome KIND with no `ok` field and carries `drainRequired: true` and `versionDelta: 0`. A test asserting "refused with code X" for the ACTIVE-cancellation cell will fail against correct behaviour and may push a worker to change production instead of the test.
2. THE FOUR ADMITTED CELLS ARE A CEILING, NOT A FLOOR. MAX_TURNS_EXHAUSTED and REFUSED are terminal facts that must NOT become FAILED. Give that its own named test; it is the cell a future reader will most plausibly "correct".
3. REDUCER REFUSALS MUST BE CARRIED, NOT RESTAMPED. DoD 3 requires the reducer's original SupervisorFailure code and layer to survive — assert BOTH fields on the terminal-absorption case, because a code-only assertion stays green if this module starts restamping the layer.
4. THE ACCEPTED CONTROL CAN GO TAUTOLOGICAL. If the expected `settlementDigest` is computed by calling the production helper, the assertion tests nothing. Derive it independently from the seeded observation.
5. THE 120-CASE SWEEP CAN GO VACUOUS. Generate it from the frozen vocabularies imported through the public root and assert the count is exactly 120 and nonzero — a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes every arm.
6. `expectTypeOf` does not execute in this suite. A type-level claim pinned that way is decoration.
7. Two ratchet axes at index-surface.test.ts:374 — the count literal AND the sorted list. Bumping only the count produces an array-diff failure that reads like an unrelated regression.
8. effect-lifecycle.ts (262) and effect-kernel.ts (266) are both ALREADY over the 250 target. Do not add to either; the new module must carry everything, and split to a sibling contracts module if it crosses 250 itself.
9. Mutation drill (i) has to ADD a field to the input type before it can trust a caller target — that is expected, and it is precisely what proves the unrepresentable-by-construction claim rather than a validated-away one.
10. Drills run in a shared worktree; snapshot hashes and restore by content, never `git checkout`.
